items.title: Cathie Wood and 8 Other Big Funds Bought Airbnb Last Quarter. Ken Fisher and 11 Others Sold. Who’s Right?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysOf the 460 big funds that have filed 13Fs for the third quarter, nine bought Airbnb, including Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest, and 12 sold, including Ken Fisher’s Fisher Investments. The sellers moved far more money, but two of the three biggest still own large Airbnb stakes, and Fisher sold only 1,600 shares.

items.title: BI Survey: Budgetary Constraints for 2027 Travel
items.summary:
Jody Lurie, Bloomberg Intelligence Credit Analyst, discussed her recent Bloomberg Survey covering budgetary constraints for 2027 travel. Lurie spoke with Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu.on her recent BI surveys.
US vacationers appear poised to spend more in 2027, but inflation is reshaping rather than curbing demand as higher core trip costs squeeze spending on extras, based on Bloomberg Intelligence's seventh US travel survey conducted Oct. 26-Nov. 4. About 71% believe they'll spend more, but only 45% would absorb higher-than-expected costs vs. 50% two years ago, while 53% cite inflation as a reason for bigger budgets. This shift favors midtier hotels and pressures airline and cruise upselling, while generative AI is a nearer-term threat to deal-hunting than booking for Expedia, Booking Holdings and Airbnb.

items.title: Will Raised Revenue Guidance Change Expedia's (EXPE) Narrative
items.summary: Expedia Group reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$4,938 million and net income of US$1,030 million, affirmed a US$0.48 quarterly dividend that was paid on December 10, 2026, and raised full year revenue guidance to a range of US$16.37 billion to US$16.43 billion. The combination of higher full year and fourth quarter 2026 revenue guidance, stronger year to date earnings and an ongoing dividend indicates that Expedia Group is focusing on both reinvestment capacity and direct cash returns...
